REGISTERED ESTABLISHMENT
EXPORT REGISTRATION RECORD
1. Establishment Details
2. Registered Export Operations

This establishment is registered to conduct export operations for barley (grain). All export activities carried out at this premises are within the registered scope as approved by the Department of Agriculture, Fisheries and Forestry (DAFF).
3. Registration Status

Registration RE-VIC-2022-0188 is current and active. The establishment was granted registration on 24 October 2022 and the current registration period extends to 23 October 2025. There are no conditions, suspensions or reviews attached to this registration.
4. Fit and Proper Person

Ingrid Sorensen is the nominated responsible person for this registration. The establishment has been under continuous management since 2014. The entity is a proprietary company registered with ASIC. The responsible person has completed the DAFF Export Compliance Fundamentals training and holds current industry accreditation.
5. Registered Premises — Area Description

The registered premises comprise Lot 38 on Plan DP 276396, located at 55 Sunraysia Highway, Donald VIC 3480. The total registered area is 41.7 hectares. The registered boundary is delineated on the attached site plan (Appendix A) and includes all receival, storage, processing and dispatch infrastructure. Adjoining land parcels and access roads are excluded from the registered area.
6. Features, Facilities and Adjoining Sites
6.1 Buildings and Structures
6.2 Services and Utilities
6.3 Adjoining Sites

The registered premises adjoin: (north) sealed public road; (east) cropping paddocks under same ownership; (south) state forest reserve — no stock or chemical activities; (west) neighbour's mixed-farming property — grain growing, no spray operations within 200 m.
7. Layout and Product Flow

A scaled site plan is attached at Appendix A. The plan shows the location of all receival, storage, processing and dispatch infrastructure, including silo positions, shed footprints, hardstand areas, weighbridge, access roads, and the designated export sampling point.

Product flow: barley is received at the intake pit (north hardstand), elevated to the main conveyor, and directed to either the silo complex or receival shed. Cleaned and graded product is transferred by auger to the outloading hopper for bulk dispatch. All product flow is contained within the registered area. Segregation from non-registered commodities is maintained by dedicated equipment and labelled storage zones.
8. Construction, Equipment and Facilities

The establishment infrastructure is designed and maintained to support the export of barley. Total storage capacity is approximately 3,500 tonnes. Structures are of steel-frame construction with concrete flooring throughout the grain-contact areas. Maintenance inspections are carried out annually and records held on site.
9. Notification of Changes

No changes to the registered establishment name, address, ownership, management or trading name have occurred since the last registration renewal. Should any such changes occur, DAFF will be notified in writing within the required timeframe as per Rule 4-6 of the Export Control (Plants and Plant Products) Rules 2021.
10. Alterations to Registered Premises

No structural alterations or additions to the registered premises have been carried out since the last registration approval. Any proposed alterations will be submitted to DAFF for approval prior to commencement of works, in accordance with Rule 4-5 of the Export Control (Plants and Plant Products) Rules 2021.

13. Food Safety Program

A HACCP-based food safety program is maintained for all export operations. The program addresses pre-harvest, receival, storage, processing and dispatch stages. Critical control points are documented with monitoring procedures and corrective action plans. The food safety program is reviewed annually or following any significant operational change.
14. Record Keeping

Records relating to all export operations, including receival dockets, storage logs, treatment records, dispatch documentation and audit reports, are maintained on site and in the business management system. Records are retained for a minimum of two years from the date of the relevant export activity in accordance with Rule 4-7B of the Export Control (Plants and Plant Products) Rules 2021.

5. HACCP Control Chart — Monitoring and Corrective Action
6. Hygiene and Waste Controls (Checking Point 3.1)

Hygiene and Sanitation Program (NQGT-HSP-001):
• Terminal cleaning: receival pit cleaned weekly; conveyor gallery swept daily; elevator boots washed monthly.
• Between commodities: blow-down of all conveyors and elevator legs before changing grain type.
• Vessel loading spout cleaned after each vessel loading.
• Personnel: safety footwear and dust masks required in operational areas; handwash on entry.
• Records: Cleaning Register (NQGT-CLN-01).

Waste Management Procedure (NQGT-WMP-001):
• Screenings: scalper waste in sealed skip; removed by contractor to composting monthly.
• Grain dust: cyclone collector emptied weekly; removed to composting.
• Vessel hold washings: water + grain residues pumped to shore reception; disposed per port environmental regulations.
• Chemical waste: fumigant sachets disposed per APVMA requirements.
7. Pest Control (Checking Point 3.2)

Pest Control Program (NQGT-PCP-001):
• 12 internal bait stations (Bromadiolone) in terminal building.
• Insect pitfall traps in 4 export silos.
• Phosphine fumigation available on request.
⚠ DEFICIENCY: No monitoring schedule specifying inspection frequency. No corrective action procedure if rodent activity or insect infestation is detected. Pest effectiveness CANNOT be demonstrated without documented monitoring records and corrective actions. See CCP-4 above.
ACTION: Add monitoring schedule (fortnightly inspections) and corrective action procedure.
8. Traceability and Integrity (Checking Point 4.1)

Traceability System (NQGT-TRACE-001):
• Receival dockets: grower → truck rego → weight → silo allocation.
• Silo inventory log: daily balance per silo.
• Vessel loading manifest: lists source silos, quantities, blending ratios, fumigation certificate ref.
• Retained 2 years.
9. Product Flow Chart and Failed Goods (Checking Point 4.1)
Product flow chart: see Section 3 Process Flow Diagram.

[DEFICIENCY — NOT DOCUMENTED]
No formal failed goods procedure for Port Phillip Bay Produce Pty Ltd. No documented process for segregation, re-testing, downgrade, destruction or DAFF notification.
10. Phytosanitary Security / Contamination Risk (Checking Point 4.2)

[DEFICIENCY — NOT DOCUMENTED]
No phytosanitary security section in this HACCP plan for Port Phillip Bay Produce Pty Ltd. No controls to prevent re-contamination or re-infestation between inspection and dispatch.
11. Verification and Record Keeping
Internal audit of HACCP plan: annual, by HACCP team lead.
External audit: DAFF registered establishment audit (periodic).
CCP monitoring records retained minimum 2 years.
HACCP plan reviewed following: product change, process change, new hazard identified, customer complaint, DAFF non-conformance.

FARM MANAGEMENT PLAN
Registered Establishment — Export Control (Plants and Plant Products) Rules 2021
1. OVERVIEW

Buloke Malting Barley is a registered export establishment located at 55 Sunraysia Highway, Donald VIC 3480, VIC. The establishment holds RE Number RE-VIC-2022-0188 and is registered to handle and export Cotton under the Export Control (Plants and Plant Products) Rules 2021. This Farm Management Plan documents the physical infrastructure, equipment, facilities, design standards, waste management arrangements and establishment condition relevant to compliance with Chapter 4 of the Rules and the DAFF Performance Standards IMLS-12-3742.
2. BUILDINGS AND INFRASTRUCTURE
Rules s4-2 — buildings, equipment, facilities and services required for export operations
3. EQUIPMENT AND MACHINERY
Rules s4-2(4) — equipment adequate for the type of export operations conducted
4. FACILITIES AND SERVICES
Rules s4-2 — Element 2.1 checking points C1, C2, C3
4.1 Buildings, Equipment and Facilities (C1)

The establishment has all buildings, equipment, facilities and services required for the registered export operations. Facilities are maintained in an operational condition appropriate for handling and exporting Cotton.
4.2 Lighting (C2)

LED high-bay luminaires throughout: 550 lux processing, 440 lux storage, 418 lux load-out. All levels comply with AS/NZS 1680.2.1. Photocell-activated perimeter lighting for after-hours vehicle movements.
4.3 Handwashing and Toilet Facilities (C3)

Amenities block adjacent to processing entry: 2 toilets, 2 hand basins (hot/cold, liquid soap, paper towels). Additional hand basin at packing hall entry — no-touch sensor tap, soap, paper towel roll. 'Wash hands before handling product' signage at all wash points.
5. DESIGN AND CONSTRUCTION STANDARDS
Rules s4-2(5), s4-2(6) — Element 2.2 checking points C4, C5, C6
5.1 Cleanability (C4)

Internal surfaces: smooth-finish epoxy-sealed concrete floors with 80 mm coved skirting; smooth food-grade colourbond wall linings to 2.4 m; recessed drains with stainless-steel grates. All equipment on adjustable SS feet ≥150 mm off floor. Equipment housings open fully for pressure-wash access. Cleaning schedule specifies full washdown between commodity lots.
5.2 Contamination and Pest Harbourage Minimisation (C5)

Sealed building envelope: all wall-floor junctions coved; roof-wall junctions sealed with foam backer rod and polyurethane sealant; all service penetrations sealed with expandable foam; ventilation openings fitted with 6 mm stainless wire mesh; personnel doors with 10 mm brush seals on all four sides; roller doors with rubber threshold sweeps and side brush seals. Annual pest technician inspection confirms envelope integrity.
5.3 Waste Disposal Design (C6)

Liquid waste via flush-recessed floor drains to bunded underground sump (3000 L) outside the building; pump-out by licensed contractor weekly or when 80% full. Solid waste in sealed labelled bins at designated collection points; removed to covered external waste bay daily. Dust via cyclone separator — collection bags changed fortnightly. All waste areas bunded and roofed.
6. VICSTE MANAGEMENT SYSTEM
Rules s4-7A(2)(a) — Element 3.1 checking point C7
6.1 Waste Management Procedures (C7)

Documented Waste Management Procedure (WMP-1601 Rev 1): specifies daily spillage sweep, weekly sump pump-out, post-commodity full shed washdown. Responsibilities assigned to named positions. Records in waste management log (Form WL-001) retained ≥2 years. Procedure reviewed annually by establishment manager.
Waste streams and handling arrangements:
7. ESTABLISHMENT CONDITION
Rules s4-6 — Element 3.4 (C8) and Element 3.5 (C9)
7.1 Hygiene and Cleanliness (C8)

All areas are clean and tidy at inspection. Floors swept and dry — no accumulated cotton residue, spillage or debris observed. Wall surfaces free from dust and product residue. Equipment cleaned after each production run per cleaning schedule. Amenities block clean; consumables stocked. Drain covers in place and clear.
7.2 Pest Condition (C9)

Grain insect activity identified in the cotton storage area. Probe sampling in Bin 1 on 15 February 2025 detected Sitophilus granarius (grain weevil). An infestation treatment protocol has been initiated (phosphine fumigation scheduled) but eradication has not yet been confirmed.

1. ESTABLISHMENT INFORMATION
2. SCOPE AND OBJECTIVES
Rules s4-7A(2)(a) — System of controls to manage hygiene and waste at the establishment

This plan covers all areas of Buloke Malting Barley used in grain handling and storage operations for export Sorghum. It applies to all permanent and casual employees, contractors, and visitors on site. The plan is reviewed annually or following any significant change to the establishment or operations.
Objectives of this plan:
Ensure all areas of the establishment are maintained in a clean and hygienic condition.
Prevent contamination of Sorghum during handling and export preparation.
Establish clear responsibilities for cleaning activities.
Maintain records that demonstrate ongoing compliance with hygiene requirements.
Support effective pest exclusion through hygienic site conditions.
3. PERSONNEL AND RESPONSIBILITIES
4. MASTER CLEANING SCHEDULE
Rules s4-7A(2)(a) — documented system of controls for hygiene (C1, C2)
5. AREA-SPECIFIC CLEANING PROCEDURES (SOPs)
Detailed step-by-step procedures for each area of the establishment
Receival Pit / Weighbridge

Pre-receival: Inspect pit and scale platform for residual grain from previous lot. Activate compressed air lance to dislodge grain from crevices, joints and conveyor housings. Sweep accumulated grain into collection bin. Wipe scale display and control panel with damp cloth. Supervisor to sign pre-loading checklist before grain intake commences.
Elevator Boot & Leg Casings

At end of each operating day: Lock out elevator drive before opening access hatch. Using industrial vacuum, extract all dead-stock grain from boot throat, casing joints, and transition points. Inspect internal surfaces for grain bridges or insect webbing. Record any pest signs in the Pest Monitoring Log. Replace and secure access hatch. Enter completed task in Equipment Cleaning Log.
Belt Conveyors & Augers

Weekly maintenance cleaning: Isolate drive motor and lock out before commencing. Run conveyor empty for five minutes to clear carrying strand. Remove belt guards and clean all carry rollers and return rollers with a stiff brush. Vacuum accumulated grain and dust from trough pan. Inspect belt splice and edges for wear. Reassemble all guards before returning to service. Record in Cleaning Log.
Grain Storage Silos / Bins

Between commodity lots: Full physical inspection and clean-out required before loading a new grain lot. Access silo through roof hatch or side door (confined space procedure applies). Sweep-out all surfaces using long-handled broom. Vacuum residue from cone and floor. Inspect walls and roof for webbing, insect activity, or mould. Record findings on Pre-Loading Checklist. Silo must not be loaded until the checklist is signed by the Storage Manager.
Grain Screening / Cleaning Plant

Designated staff are responsible for maintaining the Grain Screening / Cleaning Plant in a clean and hygienic condition following each production run or daily as scheduled. Appropriate cleaning agents at specified dilutions shall be used. Completed cleaning activities are to be recorded in the site cleaning log.
6. MANAGEMENT OF RESIDUES AND DEAD-STOCK ZONES

Particular attention is given to dead-stock zones in elevator boots, conveyor transition points, and auger troughs. These areas accumulate grain that cannot self-clear during normal operation and provide harbouring conditions for stored product insects. Full physical extraction is required at each lot change.
7. APPROVED CLEANING CHEMICAL REGISTER
All chemicals must be used at specified dilutions. Safety Data Sheets (SDS) maintained on site.
8. RECORD-KEEPING SYSTEM
Rules s4-7A(2)(a) — records to demonstrate compliance (C3, C4)
8.1 Record System

The establishment operates a digital hygiene management system (AgriCompliance Pro) for recording all cleaning activities. Paper originals are scanned and archived within 48 hours. Records are retained for a minimum of two years and are available for audit on request.
8.2 Sanitation Verification Log Template
9. VERIFICATION PROCEDURES

The establishment manager or nominated supervisor conducts a visual inspection of all cleaned areas prior to production commencement. Any deficiency identified is corrected before the area is cleared for use.
10. NON-CONFORMANCE AND CORRECTIVE ACTION

Where a cleaning deficiency is identified, the affected area is immediately re-cleaned before any product handling recommences. The deficiency, cause, and corrective action taken are recorded in the Non-Conformance Register. Repeat occurrences trigger a review of the relevant SOP.
11. ESTABLISHMENT CONDITION ASSESSMENT
Rules s4-6 — establishment to be maintained in a condition appropriate for export operations (C5)

At the most recent internal inspection (25 February 2025), all areas of Buloke Malting Barley were found to be in a clean and hygienic condition consistent with the requirements of this plan. No deficiencies were identified.
